update.current: up to date on the {channel} channel

cert.title: The device's certificate changed
cert.body: WatchLog stopped reading this device: the certificate it shows isn't the one WatchLog pinned. That happens after a reset or a new certificate, and also when something sits between WatchLog and the device. Check the fingerprint on the device before accepting it.
cert.acceptedTitle: A new certificate was accepted for this device
cert.acceptedBody: If that was a mistake, an Owner can undo it: the certificate pinned before is pinned again. If the device still shows the new one, WatchLog stops reading it until an Owner decides, as before the accept.

tiles.calculatingSub: needs an hour of its write rate

panel.title: Ports

netDevice.noPorts: No ports read yet: they appear after the first poll.

charts.empty: No data in this time range.

stack.title: Stack

settings.title: Manage
settings.loadError: The pollers and profiles couldn't be loaded.
settings.name: Name
settings.saved: Saved. The poller picks it up within a minute.
settings.removeHint: Removing stops polling it and takes its links and endpoints off the map. Its history stays until retention ends, and adding the same address again brings the device back with it.
settings.removeLine: WatchLog stops polling it, and its links and endpoints leave the map.
settings.managedAp: CAPsMAN manages this access point: WatchLog reads it through its controller, from the controller's poller and profile.
settings.addressHint: Where the poller reaches it. Its history stays; a certificate is pinned again on first contact.
settings.addressSaved: Saved. It is read at the new address from the next poll.
settings.pauseHint: Pausing stops WatchLog reading this device, and its alerts rest. Its history, links and place on the map stay. Use it for planned work on the device.
settings.pausedHint: Polling is paused: WatchLog isn't reading this device and its alerts rest. Its history stays.
settings.pausedNow: Paused. The poller stops reading it within a minute.
settings.resumed: Resumed. It is read again from the next poll.

elsewhere.ap: Its radios, clients and signal are on the Wireless page.
elsewhere.nas: Its disks, volumes and iSCSI LUNs are on the Storage page.
elsewhere.nvr: Its recording, cameras and disks are on the Storage page.
elsewhere.ups: Its battery, load and what it feeds are on the Storage page.

netDevice.openAlerts: no open alerts | {n} open alert | {n} open alerts

netAdd.title: Add network devices
netAdd.readOnly: WatchLog only reads. It never changes a device's settings, and it sweeps an address range only when you give one.
netAdd.viewer: Only Owners and Admins add network devices and change credential profiles. You can see the profiles here; their secrets are never shown to anyone.
netAdd.loadError: The pollers and profiles couldn't be loaded.

poller.title: Read them from where?
poller.intro: A collector inside your network reads the devices, so nothing on them is opened to the internet.
poller.none: No cluster or Server fleet yet. Add one first, then come back here.
poller.kubernetesLong: Kubernetes cluster · its collector polls from inside the cluster
poller.kubernetesNoCollector: Its collector hasn't reported yet: update the agent in this cluster.
poller.serverLong: a server of the fleet {fleet} · polls from this server
poller.noServers: No server in this fleet yet.
poller.noCollector: The collector isn't on this server yet.
poller.notReporting: Its collector hasn't reported in the last 10 minutes.
poller.install: Run this on {host} to add the collector; it updates the agent in place.
poller.moveThem: Move it to another poller… | Move them to another poller…
poller.moveTo: Read this device of {name} from | Read these {n} devices of {name} from
poller.moveChoose: Choose a cluster or a server
poller.moveHint: They are read from there from the next poll. Their history and profiles stay; a paused device stays paused.

cred.title: Read-only credentials
cred.intro: Tick the profiles to try on each address (up to {n}). Each device is read with the first one that answers.
cred.usedBy: used by {n} device | used by {n} devices
cred.byAddress: Recorders are added by address, below.
cred.name: Profile name
cred.keyHint: At least 8 characters. Never shown again after you save.
cred.v2cNote: SNMP v2c sends the community string in clear text over the network. Use it only where v3 isn't possible, on a network you trust.

transportsHint.rest: RouterOS 7: the web service over HTTPS. Recommended.

cred.plainWarning: The plain API sends the password in clear text. Anyone on the path between the poller and the router can read it.
cred.httpsHint: Its certificate is pinned on first contact, as for RouterOS; a changed certificate stops polling until an Owner accepts it.
cred.httpHint: Plain HTTP: digest authentication keeps the password off the wire, but what the recorder answers is readable on the way.
cred.badPort: The port is a number from 1 to 65535.
cred.stored: Stored encrypted; never shown again after you save.
cred.needKeys: SNMPv3 needs both keys, at least 8 characters each.
cred.needAllowPlain: Tick “Allow unencrypted on this network” to use the plain API.
cred.savedNote: {name} is saved. Its devices are read with the new values from the next poll.
cred.keepHint: Leave empty to keep the current one
cred.protocolFixed: A profile's protocol can't change: its devices are read with it.
cred.usedNote: {n} device uses this profile. It will be read with the new values from the next poll. | {n} devices use this profile. They will be read with the new values from the next poll.

setup.title: How to make this read-only user on the device
setup.pollerHint: Limits the user to this address.
setup.pollerBad: An IPv4 or IPv6 address only.

find.title: Find the devices
find.intro: Start from a few addresses; WatchLog follows CDP, LLDP and MNDP from device to device. Devices that don't announce themselves, like a UPS or some firewalls, are added by address or by a range.
find.rangeHint: A /24 or smaller, swept at 20 addresses a second.
find.needPoller: Choose where to read them from.
find.needAddress: Give at least one address or a range.
find.tooMany: Up to 64 addresses at a time.

found.title: What was found
found.searching: Searching… nothing found yet. | Searching… {n} found so far. | Searching… {n} found so far.
found.done: Done: nothing found. | Done: {n} found. | Done: {n} found.
found.expired: The search ran out of time with nothing found. | The search ran out of time; {n} found. | The search ran out of time; {n} found.
found.name: Name

add.title: Add {n} devices | Add {n} device | Add {n} devices
add.button: Add {n} devices | Add {n} device | Add {n} devices
add.after: First data in about a minute. The network's alerts are on by default.

dahua.title: On the recorder
dahua.user: Create a user only for WatchLog, in a group with view rights only: no settings, no playback control.
dahua.network: The poller needs to reach the recorder on TCP 443 (HTTPS) or 80 (HTTP).
dahua.add: Then add the recorder by its address with this profile (step 3): recorders aren't found by discovery.

qnap.title: On the QNAP NAS (QTS)
qnap.where: Open Control Panel → Network & File Services → SNMP and turn SNMP on.
qnap.v3: Choose SNMPv3 with authentication and privacy, and a read-only user; use the same user, keys and algorithms as an SNMPv3 profile here.
qnap.network: The poller needs to reach the NAS on UDP 161.

ups.title: On the UPS
ups.where: Turn SNMP on in the UPS's network card (its web page).
ups.version: Use SNMPv3 with a read-only user, or v2c with a read-only community where v3 isn't offered.
ups.network: The poller needs to reach the network card on UDP 161.

netAdd.capsman: Wi-Fi access points managed by CAPsMAN aren't added here: they appear on their own once the router that runs CAPsMAN is added, and they don't count as devices.

recorders.title: Recorders
recorders.intro: Video recorders don't announce themselves, so discovery doesn't find them: add each one by its address with a recorder profile.
recorders.noProfile: Make a recorder profile in step 2 first (Recorder, Dahua HTTP API).
recorders.button: Add recorders | Add {n} recorder | Add {n} recorders

remove.title: Delete this credential profile?
remove.unused: No device uses it. Deleting it can't be undone; the devices' own settings are never touched.
remove.inUse: {n} device is read with this profile, so it can't be deleted yet. Move it to another profile first. | {n} devices are read with this profile, so it can't be deleted yet. Move them to another profile first.
remove.moveHint: Only profiles of the same protocol are listed. The devices are read with it from the next poll.

noOther.snmp: There is no other SNMP profile to move them to. Make one first, or edit this one instead.
noOther.routeros: There is no other RouterOS profile to move them to. Make one first, or edit this one instead.
noOther.dahua: There is no other recorder profile to move them to. Make one first, or edit this one instead.

test.title: Test against an address
test.intro: Reads one device with the values above, as typed, before anything is saved. Read-only, through the poller you choose.
test.running: Asking the poller to read it…
test.needAddress: Give the address of one device to read.
test.badAddress: That isn't an address: letters, digits, dots, colons and dashes.
test.noPoller: No poller has a collector yet: choose one in step 1 and add its collector, then test.

refused.snmp: The device answered and refused these values: the user, the authentication or the privacy key is wrong, or their protocols don't match the device's.
refused.routeros: The router answered and refused the user or the password.
refused.dahua: The recorder answered and refused the user or the password.

outcome.no_answer: Nothing answered at {address}. The address or the port may be wrong, the device may not allow this poller, or (SNMP v2c) the community is wrong: a device stays silent then.
outcome.certificate: {address} showed a certificate that isn't the one pinned for the device already added there. Nothing was sent to it. An Owner accepts a new certificate on the device's page.
outcome.plain_refused: The plain API sends the password in clear: tick "Allow unencrypted on this network" to use it.
outcome.unsupported: This poller's collector is older than 1.0.2 and can't test a recorder profile. Update it, or save the profile and add the recorder to see it answer.
outcome.poller_silent: The poller didn't report back. Is its collector running? Step 1 says when it last reported.
